html:
Olduvai Gorge is a steep ravine in the Serengeti plains of northern Tanzania, where Louis and Mary Leakey searched for early humans from 1931 and made some of the most important finds in human origins.

Layers of rock exposed by the stream hold nearly two million years of fossils and stone tools. The simple chopping tools first named here, the Oldowan, are among the oldest stone technologies known.

In 1959 Mary Leakey found the skull known as Nutcracker Man, and in 1960 her son Jonathan found remains named Homo habilis in 1964, the handy man, then seen as the first member of our genus. With Laetoli nearby, the gorge put East Africa at the centre of human evolution.
sum: Olduvai Gorge is a steep ravine in the Serengeti plains of northern Tanzania, where Louis and Mary Leakey searched for early humans from 1931 and made some of the most important finds in human origins.
